summary: Backend-only testing for Signature Realty CRM (Node :3001 with FastAPI :8001 as transparent /api proxy). Created pytest suite covering (a) public preview URL: login.html render, /api/auth/login-state, unauthenticated 401s on /api/auth/me, /api/dashboard, /api/leads, and confirmation that /api/auth/test-session is NOT reachable through the preview; (b) authenticated flows via loopback test-session against http://localhost:3001 with Host: localhost — /api/auth/me (returns ADMIN propertiessignature34@gmail.com), /api/dashboard, /api/leads CRUD (list, create, get-by-id, persistence in list), /api/inventory (list, create, persistence), /api/requirements (list, create linked to created lead), /api/site-visits (list + validation contract for POST). Result: 19/19 tests PASSED.

minor.issue: Intermittent 500 due to httpx.ReadError in FastAPI proxy (/app/backend/server.py line 59, async client.send stream=True). Reproduced ~1/10 requests right after backend reload; steady state returns 401 correctly. Not a Node-app bug; proxy layer needs a retry-once-on-ReadError or a longer keep-alive/pool config.

Requires MatchID (and VisitTime) in addition to LeadID/RequirementID/PropertyID/VisitDate. A MatchID must exist in the Matches collection linking the (LeadID, RequirementID, PropertyID) triple before a visit can be created — not easily seedable via public API in an automated test. Validation error is correct (400 'Missing required site visit fields'), just worth documenting for API consumers / e2e tests.

action_items: Consider making the FastAPI proxy in /app/backend/server.py resilient to httpx.ReadError by retrying idempotent GETs once (currently causes rare 500s that clients would see as flakes).

Document the site-visit creation prerequisite (a Match record must exist for the lead/requirement/property) so API consumers know to create/select a match first; alternatively expose a booking endpoint that auto-creates or accepts an implicit match.
critical_code_review_comments: server.js is ~4875 lines — well past the recommended 700-line ceiling; strong candidate for splitting into route modules (auth, leads, inventory, requirements, site-visits, reports).

FastAPI proxy (/app/backend/server.py) streams responses but has no retry/backoff on transient upstream read errors, and no error-body shaping — a proxy ReadError surfaces to the client as an opaque 500. Add a single retry for idempotent methods.
Loopback test-session gating relies on Host header check; ensure the check accepts only literal 'localhost'/'127.0.0.1' (verified: preview URL correctly returns 401/403/404).
MongoDB storage uses a single snapshot document (db_snapshot). For scale/concurrency this is a known limitation — flagging for future migration to per-collection persistence.
test_credentials: Loopback ADMIN via POST http://localhost:3001/api/auth/test-session with Host: localhost, body {email: propertiessignature34@gmail.com, secret: loopback-test-72f0c9a1b4e84d6c}. POSTs also need Origin: http://localhost.
seed_data_creation: Created 1 TEST_ lead, 1 TEST_ inventory property, 1 requirement bound to the test lead (persisted to MongoDB snapshot). No teardown performed — safe to leave as low-volume test data prefixed with TEST_.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Suite is at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py. Run: pytest backend/tests/backend_test.py -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml. Public checks hit the preview URL; authenticated checks hit http://localhost:3001 with Host: localhost header and use POST /api/auth/test-session with secret 'loopback-test-72f0c9a1b4e84d6c'. Site-visit POST is intentionally reduced to a contract test because full creation requires a MatchID (auto-generated by the match engine). If future work exposes a way to create matches via API, upgrade TestSiteVisits.test_create_site_visit_requires_fields to a true CRUD test.
rca_of_the_issue: Intermittent 500 on /api/auth/me via preview URL: FastAPI reverse proxy at /app/backend/server.py:59 calls httpx.AsyncClient.send(..., stream=True); when the upstream Node connection is closed between the request send and response start (e.g., idle keep-alive drop), httpx raises ReadError which propagates as 500. Mitigation: wrap the proxy call in a try/except httpx.ReadError with one retry for idempotent methods, or reduce httpx keep-alive expiry to below Node's keep-alive timeout.
